steps.tx: **Systemic lupus erythematosus** or SLE is a prototypic multisystem autoimmune disease driven by defective clearance of apoptotic cell debris. Impaired phagocytosis leads to secondary necrosis, exposing intracellular nuclear chromatin, small nuclear ribonucleoproteins, and double-stranded DNA to antigen-presenting cells, breaking immunologic self-tolerance.
steps.say: Systemic lupus erythematosus develops from defective clearance of apoptotic cell debris. Secondary necrosis exposes nuclear antigens to initiate autoimmune responses across multiple organ systems.

vis.alt: Apoptotic debris clearance defect and nuclear antigen exposure in lupus
vis.caption: Defective clearance of apoptotic debris drives autoantibody generation in SLE. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Endosomal pattern recognition receptors **TLR7** and **TLR9** within plasmacytoid dendritic cells internalise nucleic acid-containing immune complexes through surface **Fc-gamma-RIIa** or CD32. Receptor engagement triggers massive synthesis of **type I interferons** including IFN-alpha and IFN-beta, creating the characteristic pathogenic **interferon gene signature** that sustains systemic inflammation.
steps.say: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells uptake nucleic acid complexes via Fc-gamma receptor 2a. Activation of TLR7 and TLR9 stimulates high levels of type one interferon.

nodes.label: Nucleic acid immune complexes bind Fc-gamma-RIIa
Endosomal TLR7 and TLR9 receptor activation
Interferon-alpha release and interferon gene signature

steps.tx: B cell hyperreactivity and breach of humoral tolerance in SLE are driven by excess **BAFF** or B cell activating factor, alongside **APRIL**. Elevated BAFF sustains self-reactive plasma cells, promoting polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia and the emergence of pathogenic, high-affinity autoantibodies targeting nuclear structures.
steps.say: Excess BAFF and APRIL sustain autoreactive B cells and plasma cells in SLE. This cytokine excess drives persistent production of high-affinity pathogenic autoantibodies.

rows: Inhibits soluble BAFF to induce B cell apoptosis

steps.tx: Genetic susceptibility to lupus highlights early classical complement components including homozygous deficiencies of **C1q**, **C1r**, **C1s**, and **C4A/B**. Notably, homozygous **C1q deficiency** confers greater than **90 percent penetrance** of severe, early-onset cutaneous lupus erythematosus, immune complex glomerulonephritis, and severe neuropsychiatric involvement.
steps.say: Homozygous deficiency of early classical complement factors causes severe lupus. Genetic C1q deficiency confers over 90 percent penetrance of severe early-onset disease.

vis.alt: Early complement component deficiency and lupus risk
vis.caption: Early classical complement deficiency impairs clearance of apoptotic bodies, predisposing to SLE. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Dysregulated neutrophil activation generates excessive **neutrophil extracellular traps** or NETs through suicidal or vital NETosis. These traps present antimicrobial peptide LL-37, modified histones, and externalised DNA. Defective degradation by serum **DNase I** perpetuates immune complex deposition, activating endothelial cells and accelerating vascular injury in lupus nephritis.
steps.say: Exaggerated NETosis releases extracellular traps studded with histones and DNA. Impaired clearance by DNase I sustains immune complex formation and vascular endothelial injury.

rows: Prolongs tissue exposure and immune activation

steps.tx: Subendothelial and mesangial immune complex deposition triggers classical complement activation. Cleavage fragments generate anaphylatoxins **C3a** and **C5a**, recruiting inflammatory neutrophils and macrophages through Mac-1 integrins. Active inflammatory flares characteristically cause profound consumption with **depressed C3 and C4** complement levels that correlate with active disease.
steps.say: Immune complex deposition in capillaries activates classical complement. Anaphylatoxins C3a and C5a recruit leukocytes, producing tissue necrosis and dropping serum C3 and C4.

nodes.label: Immune complexes deposit in capillary walls
Classical pathway activation generates C3a and C5a
Leukocyte recruitment and hypocomplementemia with low C3/C4

steps.tx: Lupus T cells exhibit deficient interleukin-2 production, hyperactive calcium influx, and replacement of the normal T cell receptor zeta chain by the **Fc-epsilon-RI-gamma** subunit. Furthermore, suppression by CD4 positive CD25 positive **FOXP3 positive regulatory T cells** is impaired, enabling follicular helper T cells to provide unconstrained help to autoreactive B cells.
steps.say: T cells in lupus display defective interleukin-2 synthesis and rewiring of the receptor zeta chain. Impaired regulatory T cell activity permits unchecked B cell help.

right.title: Lupus T cell aberrations
points: Defective IL-2 and hyperactive calcium fluxes
Unrestrained follicular helper T cell activity

steps.tx: Environmental triggers precipitate acute flares in genetically primed hosts. Solar **ultraviolet radiation** induces keratinocyte apoptosis, causing cell-surface translocation of **Ro/SSA** and nuclear antigens. In addition, latent **Epstein-Barr virus** infection promotes autoimmunity via molecular mimicry between EBNA-1 and Sm core proteins, while estrogens enhance B cell longevity.
steps.say: Environmental triggers include ultraviolet radiation, which induces keratinocyte apoptosis and exposes Ro antigens. Epstein-Barr virus infection triggers autoimmunity through molecular mimicry.

rows: Keratinocyte apoptosis and Ro surface shift
Enhances B cell survival and prolactin release
